item.title: New Mexico Supreme Court Fines Lawyer for AI-Generated Brief with Fake Testimony
item.description:
New Mexico Supreme Court Fines Lawyer for AI-Generated Brief with Fake Testimony

The New Mexico Supreme Court has penalized lawyer Stephen Aarons for submitting an appeal for a client’s murder conviction that contained AI-fabricated witnesses and false police testimony.

⚙️ Key details

In a Wednesday filing, the court held Stephen Aarons in contempt and issued a $5,000 fine for failing to “verify the factual claims and legal authority in his AI-generated brief.”

  • Fabrications: The brief included false testimony from “wholly fabricated witnesses” and false testimony regarding the appearance and clothing of the shooter.
  • Tool Used: Aarons admitted to using ChatGPT, stating he believed it would produce a “bulletproof summary” of the trial.
  • Court Response: Justice C. Shannon Bacon questioned Aarons’ awareness of AI risks, noting that the problem of lawyers relying on “AI hallucinations” is an “above-the-fold story every single day.”
  • Defense: In a statement to Reuters, Aarons said, “I am remorseful but hopeful that the disciplinary board takes into account it was an honest mistake.”

💡 Why it matters

This incident follows other legal cases involving AI-generated inaccuracies:
